elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: The inserted covenant addresses only professional liability (E&O) and cyber/privacy liability; no commercial general liability per-occurrence limit appears anywhere in the rendered language.

elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.
elements.evidence: No CGL aggregate limit is stated; the insertion contains no general liability coverage at all.

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted text sets E&O at 'not less than USD 1,000,000', below the preferred USD 2,000,000 threshold.

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: Condition applies (Garman converts and handles Sparkling data at Authorized Locations), but cyber and privacy cover is set at USD 2,000,000, short of USD 5,000,000.

elements.element: Vendor maintains workers' compensation coverage as required by law.
elements.evidence: No workers' compensation obligation appears in the inserted paragraph or elsewhere in the rendered language.

elements.element: Vendor provides certificates of insurance on request.
elements.evidence: No certificate-of-insurance delivery mechanic is included in the insertion.

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: 'Garman shall maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000' — express, unconditional covenant at the fallback amount.

elements.element: Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: '... and cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000' — express covenant matching the fallback threshold.

reasons: The rule is correctly classified as missing: the rendered operative language shows no pre-existing insurance covenant in the General Matters provisions, and the vendor installs Software and converts data at Authorized Locations, so the absence is walk-away territory.

Fallback level is complete: both atomic elements (E&O not less than USD 1,000,000; cyber and privacy not less than USD 2,000,000) appear as an unconditional Vendor covenant in operative text, not merely promised in the margin comment.

Preferred level is not complete — CGL per-occurrence and aggregate limits, E&O at USD 2,000,000, cyber at USD 5,000,000, workers' compensation and certificates on request are all absent. To reach preferred, the drafter would need to add CGL USD 1,000,000 per occurrence / USD 2,000,000 aggregate, raise E&O to USD 2,000,000, raise cyber to USD 5,000,000, add statutory workers' compensation, and add a certificates-on-request sentence.

Minimality holds: the insertion is a single sentence limited to the two selected fallback elements. It correctly omits model-language extras that the fallback checklist does not require — 'at its own expense', the term-plus-one-year survival tail, CGL, and the certificate mechanic — each of which would have been a non-minimal addition. No existing wording (including the assignment and headings provisions) was deleted or paraphrased.

Intent is preserved: the new covenant is a standalone obligation that creates no undefined terms, no dangling cross-references, and no contradiction with retained assignment, installation, or interpretation language; unrelated allocation, timing and commercial mechanics survive intact.
